question.text: Compared to a typical mutual fund, a Cat III AIF following a Long-Short Strategy differs PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: MF can run 130/30 freely; Cat III cannot short.
Cat III permits short selling and 2x leverage, while MFs have far more restrictive short and leverage rules.
Cat III is open to retail; MF is HNI-only.
Both are identically regulated under SEBI (MF) Regulations.

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs may follow long-only or long-short strategies, including short positions through options and futures (e.g., 130/30-style exposure), and their leverage must not exceed 2 times NAV. Mutual funds are described as traditional collective investment vehicles where leverage is not allowed. The Trap: Saying MFs can run 130/30 freely while Cat III cannot short inverts the regime; Cat III is not open to retail in the same way as MFs; MFs and AIFs are governed by separate SEBI regulations. Note: The contrast turns on Cat III's permission to use long-short strategies with leverage up to 2x NAV versus the no-leverage framing applied to mutual funds.
